issue.title: Email unsubscribe link is generated as a relative URL
issue.reason:
`Topic#unsubscribe_url` extends the topic's site-relative `url` and the mailer passes that value directly into the email translation. The resulting email link lacks the site origin, so external email clients cannot reliably resolve it to the Discourse installation.
Evidence: PRF014 constructs the unsubscribe URL solely from `Topic#url`; PRF009 passes it unchanged as `unsubscribe_url`; PRF001 inserts that value directly into Markdown link syntax; and PRF002 cooks the translation into email HTML without making the URL absolute.
Business impact: Recipients may receive a per-topic unsubscribe link that is broken or points at the email provider rather than the Discourse site, preventing the advertised unsubscribe flow.
Also affects: app/mailers/user_notifications.rb, config/locales/server.en.yml, lib/email/message_builder.rb
issue.suggestedFixDescription: Generate an absolute URL before it reaches the email template, for example by prefixing the topic path with `Discourse.base_url` in `Topic#unsubscribe_url` or by passing an absolute URL from the mailer. Add an email-rendering assertion that the resulting `href` contains the forum origin.
issue.hypothesis: When a notification email is generated, `%{unsubscribe_url}` becomes a path such as `/t/example/123/unsubscribe`; because an email message has no dependable document base URL, following the rendered link fails or resolves against the mail client's own origin.

raw_assessment.reason: Topic#url delegates to Topic.url, which starts with Discourse.base_url. Topic#unsubscribe_url appends /unsubscribe to that absolute URL, and the mailer passes it unchanged as unsubscribe_url. Therefore the generated email link includes the forum origin rather than being site-relative.
